author: Declaration Desk
title: Gukesh and Sindarov draw again in 20 moves; world title match level at 1-1
dek: The champion tried the London System with White but the challenger held comfortably. Sindarov has White in Game 3 tonight.
body:
D. Gukesh and Javokhir Sindarov drew Game 2 of the World Chess Championship in Geneva on Wednesday in just 20 moves, leaving the 14-game match level at 1-1.

With White for the first time in the match, Gukesh opened with 1.d4 and the London System, a choice he had not made before at this level. Sindarov again played quickly in the opening, and Gukesh, who fell behind on the clock in Game 1 as well, spent long periods over several moves, including 25 minutes after Sindarov's surprising 11...Qd8 and 30 minutes on 16.f3. Sindarov's active set-up with ...f5 left White with no obvious way forward, and the game ended in a draw by threefold repetition.

"I'd have preferred both results go my way!" Gukesh said afterwards, according to the event's official reporting. Sindarov said of his time advantage: "When my opponent thinks, I'm just trying to chill!"

Game 3 begins at 7.30 pm IST on Thursday, with Sindarov playing White, before the first rest day on Friday. The first player to 7.5 points wins the title; a 7-7 score would go to rapid tie-breaks. The match carries a prize fund of $2.5 million.
